marta: Quick heads-up — after the CUDA driver roll to 536.10 last night some H100 clusters started picking a different kernel path for mid-long sequences. We see p50 ~+10% and p95 ~+35% on /v1/generate (seq 512 warm -> 1024 continuation). Sharing the lightweight profile we ran.
perf-bot: [ALERT] 2026-11-12T03:12Z p95 increase on route /v1/generate in h100-prod (canary group). Baseline: 48ms -> 65ms. Top affected kernels: mha_mm_sm80_fast (new pick), kvcache_copy_slow. Trace id: trace_180450_1
liam: Do we have a repro locally? which kernel pick changed exactly? can you paste the autotuner decision blob?
marta: repro on canary is trivial with synthetic load: `make perf-run ARGS=\"--seq-warm=512 --seq-cont=1024 --batch=1\"` — profiler snippet:
```
--- profiler snippet ---
seq 512 warm -> 1024 cont
old driver (535.xx) kernel picks:
  mha_kernel_sm80_opt (60%), mha_fused_kv (30%), kvcache_copy_fast (10%)
new driver (536.10) kernel picks:
  mha_kernel_sm80_opt (10%), mha_kernel_sm80_fast (70%), kvcache_copy_slow (20%)
observations: mha_kernel_sm80_fast has lower FLOP-eff but worse memory layout for this seq pattern; kvcache_copy_slow has +1.8x memcpy cost
p95 latency delta: +35%
```
sasha: ugh. looks like the autotuner scoring shifted — likely due to reported clock/occupancy changes in the new driver. any config to force old kernel while we investigate? we should also check batching heuristics — maybe continuous batching changed thresholds.
ryan: We can short-term force a chosen kernel with `REDEX_RUNTIME_FORCE_KERNEL=mha_kernel_sm80_opt` per process env on the serving pool. Suggest rolling that to the affected canary pool first. Also add an automatic fallback: if p95 goes >20% over baseline for 5m, set env override via rollout controller.
devon: I can push a tiny canary with env override and a microbench script. microbench command:
```
# run inside runtime container
python -m perf_bench.run --model redwood/xxl --seq-warm 512 --seq-cont 1024 --iters 100 --concurrency 8
```
I'll also attach a kernel-pick dump `runtime --dump-autotune > /tmp/kinv.json`
liam: Good. Also please grab nvprof/cupti traces for a single request to see occupancy and sm_eff for the two kernels. Might be that the new driver exposes a different occupancy heuristic to cupti and that confuses our cost model.
marta: grabbing traces now. quick note: kvcache behavior looked worse under mixed-size batching; we saw extra memcpy for cache warm hits. probable regression in our memcpy path interacting with driver pinned memory behavior.
perf-bot: [ANOMALY] kvcache hit ratio stable but avg kvcopy latency increased 2x at 03:00Z — correlates with driver rollout window.
sasha: Plan proposal:
  1) roll env override to canary (marta/devon) — force old kernel pick
  2) collect nvprof traces + autotune dumps (liam)
  3) run microbench matrix across seq lengths [64,128,256,512,1024] and batch sizes [1,4,8]
  4) if rollback to driver <536.10 possible in affected region -> schedule immediate rollback window (ops)
  5) medium-term: make autotuner robust to minor occupancy deltas by adding hysteresis and a cost-smoothing window (research)
ryan: +1. I'll prepare rollout flags and the 5min degrade -> auto-override hook. Also will open a short-term incident with ops to hold the driver upgrade in other clusters until we confirm.
marta: doing the canary override now and will post results. tagging @liam @sasha for traces when ready. :thumbsup:
devon: kicked microbench, will post raw numbers in-thread shortly.
liam: thanks team. once we have nvprof traces we'll compare kernel SM/util and L2 throughput. If it's just driver reporting differences we can patch cost model quickly. If it's real perf regression from memcpy path we may need rollback.
marta: update: canary override dropped p95 back to baseline within 2 runs. nvprof capture scheduled. will dump autotune blobs to /artifacts/180450/ and link here when ready.
